Visibility-Based Pruning removes 3D scene elements (points, voxels, or Gaussians) by analyzing their visibility across a set of training camera viewpoints, minimizing rendering distortion while maintaining object watertightness [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly describes a pruning technique that removes 3D scene elements (specifically points, though the claim generalizes to voxels/Gaussians which the source notes can be adapted for) based on visibility across training camera viewpoints. It confirms that this process minimizes rendering distortion (by removing points occluded by most viewpoints) and maintains object watertightness (as stated in Section III). The specific mechanisms described in the claim (analyzing visibility, minimizing distortion, maintaining watertightness) are all present in the provided text.
